newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka reports 200 rebel casualties in assault.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka reports 200 rebel casualties in assault.

text.p: More than 200 Tamil Tiger rebels were believed killed or wounded by Sri Lankan troops in their fresh strike on northern guerrilla territory on Sunday, the defence ministry said on Monday.
"Ground troops and terrorist transmissions indicated over 200 casualties among the terrorists," a ministry statement said.

In its first official confirmation of the military's renewed push into the rebel-held town of Kilinochchi, the ministry said ground troops backed by armour, artillery and air force bombers faced heavy rebel resistance.

Sunday's offensive was the first major attack in more than a month by the troops who had consolidated positions around the junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, a gateway to the rebels' jungle territory of Wanni.

The separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), which seeks an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, earlier this year lost their stronghold of the Jaffna peninsula which they had ruled for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.
The statement said at least 21 government soldiers were killed and 58 wounded in Sunday's action. A military officer earlier put the death toll at 30 by Monday morning.
